name: image3
caption: The hypothalamic–pituitary axis regulates the release of hormones.

name: image4
caption: An example of negative feedback. Circulating thyroid hormone (TH) levels (T3 \+ T4) alert the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary to increase or decrease thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) secretion.

name: image5
caption: An example of positive feedback. Oxytocin levels during labor and delivery increase release of additional oxytocin until the birth of the baby, which decreases stretching of the cervix and the cycle is interrupted.

name: image6
caption: Two types of hormone–receptor interactions: (A) the surface receptor and (B) the intracellular receptor.

name: image8

name: image9

name: image15
caption: The adrenal glands are positioned above each kidney and have an outer adrenal cortex and an inner adrenal medulla. Hormones from the adrenal cortex include mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, androgens, and estrogens. Hormones from the adrenal medulla are epinephrine and norepinephrine.
